item.title: Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now
item.description:

item.title: Jeff Bezos says he was ‘heavily involved’ in picking the new James Bond
item.description:
Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond made enough sense given his recent work with director Denis Villeneuve, who's making the franchise's next film over at Amazon. But it turns out that Amazon founder Jeff Bezos played a significant role in making the final decision, too.

item.description:

item.title: iFixit’s Apple HomeView teardown reveals a device that will be difficult to repair
item.description:
After finding recent versions of Apple's iPads and HomePods much easier to disassemble for battery replacements or other repairs, iFixit assumed it would be the same story for Apple's new HomeView hub that looks like a seven-inch tablet stuck to a smart speaker. The reality was much different and by the time they got the HomeView apart iFixit's skilled techs had "ripped a connector, snapped a speaker in two, and put more force on the poor logic board than any of us were comfortable with."

item.title: Nvidia says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
item.description:
Starting Nvidia's quarterly earnings call on Tuesday, new board chair Harvey Jones said that when former CEO Jensen Huang resigned, "the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."

item.title: The MacBook Neo is receiving a rare $50 discount ahead of Black Friday
item.description:
If you’re looking for a new laptop or a gift for the student in your life, you can save $50 on the MacBook Neo at several retailers, in both storage sizes and all four colors. The 256GB model is currently discounted to $649 (Amazon, Best Buy, Target), while the 512GB model with Touch ID is down to $749 (Amazon, Best Buy, Target). None of the retailers currently list an end date for the discount, which is the biggest price drop we’ve seen since Apple raised the laptop’s MSRP by $100 in July in response to the ongoing RAM crisis.

MacBook Neo

Where to Buy:

  • $799 $749 at Amazon (512GB)
  • $699 $649 at Best Buy (256GB)
  • $699 $649 at Amazon (256GB)

Apple’s budget-friendly MacBook leverages the A18 Pro processor, a chip originally found in the iPhone 16 Pro, to keep costs down. Both the 256GB and 512GB models feature 8GB of memory, and my colleague Antonio G. Di Benedetto was impressed by the vivid 13-inch screen and speakers, the latter of which are better than those in many cheap (and even midrange) Windows laptops. The Neo isn’t super performant, especially in terms of storage speed and total memory, but it’s great for everyday tasks, casual use, and students.

Read our Apple MacBook Neo review.

item.title: Nike’s new air sole technology can mix soft and firm cushioning
item.description:
In 2024, Nike announced its Air Max 1000 that were manufactured using a 3D-printing process resulting in a shoe that had a uniform silhouette but varying areas of support and flexibility throughout. The company is now doing something similar with its iconic air-filled soles using its new Tuned Air technology. While previously the level of cushioning in Nike Air shoes was uniform across the entire sole, a new manufacturing process can produce multiple air pockets with varying levels of cushioning and stability.

item.title: Not even Sam Altman is safe from AI deepfakes on Instagram
item.description:
Instagram is filled with people posting deepfaked content - including, as of late, from one of Meta's most prominent executives.

item.title: Instagram is helping creators crack down on copycat videos
item.description:
Instagram is beginning to roll out a "content protection" feature that lets creators see and review copies of their videos posted to the platform.

"For eligible creators who enroll, content protection is a tool that automatically looks out for visual matches of your original videos, alerts you when we find a match across Instagram and Facebook, and lets you decide what happens next," Meta says in a blog post. Meta launched a similar tool for Facebook last year to help users "safeguard" their Reels and "maintain control" over their creative work.
